newsitem.title: USA: Orion to buy last interest in partnership.
newsitem.headline: Orion to buy last interest in partnership.

text.p: Orion Network Systems Inc said it had agreed to acquire all of the interests that it did not already own in the Orion Atlantic partnership.
Orion, which already owns 41.7 percent of the partnership, said it would swap about $122 million of convertible preferred stock for the remaining interest.
The preferred stock will be convertible into common stock at $17.50 per share, representing about 7.0 million common shares, it said.
The acquisition, which is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 1997, is subject to the refinancing of about $210 million of existing Orion Atlantic partnership bank debt.
In connection with the deal, partner British Aerospace Plc will invest about $50 million in convertible securities of Orion, representing about 3.5 million common shares, it said.

Orion also said it had signed a contract with Matra Marconi Space to build and launch a satellite that will provide expanded capacity and coverage of Europe, Russia, South America and the eastern United States.
It said it planned to arrange financing for the satellite by the second quarter of 1998.

Orion Atlantic, a limited partnership formed in 1991 to construct, launch and operate communications satellites over the Atlantic Ocean, includes partners like ComDev, Kingston Communications, Lockheed Martin Corp, Matra Hachette and Nissho Iwai Corp.

Orion Network Systems is an international satellite communications company that provides private, multimedia, network communications services directly to multinational businesses via small receiving antennas which bypass terrestrial infrastructures.
